item.title: Back-to-school vaccination reminder
item.description:
Back-to-school vaccination reminder jenniferdhogan Wed, 09/02/2026 - 12:41

As the new school year approaches, the Chief Public Health Office is reminding parents and guardians to check their children's immunization records and make an appointment with Public Health Nursing if vaccinations are not up to date.

Vaccination remains one of the safest and most effective ways to protect children from serious illnesses. Keeping immunizations up to date helps children stay healthy at school, at home and in their communities.

"A new school year is an exciting time for children and families,” said Chief Public Health Officer Dr. Heather Morrison. “Making sure routine vaccinations are up to date is one of the best ways to protect children from preventable diseases and support healthy schools across Prince Edward Island." 

Routine childhood vaccines are provided free through public health nursing offices across the province, helping to protect against diseases including:

  • Diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis (whooping cough)
  • Polio
  • Measles, mumps and rubella
  • Meningococcal disease
  • Varicella (chickenpox)

Each year, public health nurses travel to Island schools to provide the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to all grade 6 students. HPV in-school catch-up clinics were also offered in 2025-26 for students in Grade 12. Through these two initiatives, almost 90% of graduating students last year received their HPV vaccine.

Public health nurses also offer school-based immunization clinics for Grade 9 students. These clinics provide vaccines that protect against tetanus, diphtheria and pertussis (Tdap), meningococcal disease and other vaccine-preventable illnesses as part of PEI's routine immunization program.

Beginning in the 2026-27 school year, Grade 12 students will be offered catch-up opportunities for routine publicly funded vaccines through school-based clinics. This initiative will help ensure students are up to date on recommended immunizations before graduation. In addition, the meningococcal B (Men-B) vaccine is available to Grade 12 students who are planning to attend a post-secondary institution or join the military.

Public Health encourages families to follow PEI's routine immunization schedule to ensure children receive recommended vaccines on time and have the best possible protection against vaccine-preventable diseases.

"PEI has a very strong immunization program. We know families have a lot on their minds as a new school year approaches, so to help make immunization as accessible as possible, PEI offers recommended childhood vaccines free through public health nursing Island wide. Keeping vaccinations up to date is an easy step that families can take to help protect their children and support healthy schools and communities.” 

- Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle

Parents or guardians can contact a local Public Health Nursing office to have their child's immunization record reviewed and to schedule any missed vaccinations.

Families are also encouraged to receive recommended seasonal vaccines, including influenza and COVID-19 vaccines, when they become available this fall.

More information is available at Childhood Immunizations.

item.title: Affordable rural transit helps students get to campus
item.description:
Affordable rural transit helps students get to campus jenniferdhogan Tue, 09/01/2026 - 13:22

As thousands of post-secondary students prepare for the fall semester, the province is reminding students in rural communities that public transit can provide a convenient and affordable ride to campus.

Transit PEI connects communities across Prince Edward Island to Charlottetown, Summerside, Georgetown and other regional centres every weekday (Mon - Fri). 

“Rural transit gives Island students another option for getting to and from school. It’s a convenient, safe and affordable way to travel.”

- Transportation, Infrastructure and Energy Minister Ernie Hudson

For students, choosing transit can mean spending less money on gas, parking, vehicle maintenance and other costs associated with driving. Post-secondary students can purchase a monthly pass for $10. A single trip costs $2. 

Full-time UPEI students have access to the T3 Transit network through the U-Pass included with tuition. 

Due to the popularity of the service, students are encouraged to review their route and reserve their seats as early as possible.  Since January, ridership on rural transit routes has increased by more than 4 per cent year over year. 

Bookings should be made at least three hours before travel and can be secured up to 30 days in advance. Recurring bookings are also available for students who follow a regular class schedule. 

Online bookings can be made at T3 Rural Transit Schedules 

Quick facts:

  • Average daily ridership for rural transit in 2025 was almost 600 one-way passenger trips, excluding the seasonal north shore route.
  • Local and intercommunity transit services link workers to jobs, students to schools, shoppers to businesses, and Islanders to the essential services they need to enhance their quality of life.
  • The North Shore summer shuttle service became a permanent service in 2025. This summer, more runs were added to give riders more options in the evening.

item.title: New framework for chronic disease prevention and care
item.description:
New framework for chronic disease prevention and care jenniferdhogan Tue, 09/01/2026 - 10:06

The province is launching a new framework to guide efforts to reduce the impact of chronic disease in Prince Edward Island and help Islanders live longer, healthier lives.

The Chronic Disease Framework is a province-wide approach that brings together government, healthcare and community partners, and Islanders to help people stay healthy, prevent chronic disease where possible and improve coordinated care for those living with chronic disease. It will guide future policies, strategies, and services through three pillars: prevention; screening and early detection; and disease management.

"Chronic disease affects thousands of people and it's one of the biggest pressures on our health system. We want Islanders to have the best possible health and quality of life, and we want those living with chronic diseases to have the support and resources they need to manage their health. This framework gives us a roadmap to do that work together."

- Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle

Chronic diseases account for seven of the 10 leading causes of death in Prince Edward Island and Canada. Many chronic diseases have shared risk factors, and evidence-based management and coordinated care can improve prevention, early detection, and long-term health outcomes. 

“This framework reinforces our commitment to providing person-centred care that supports Islanders at every stage of chronic disease prevention and management," said Health PEI interim Chief Executive Officer Laurae Kloschinsky. "By strengthening coordination across healthcare services and working closely with community partners, we can help Islanders access the right care and support at the right time and make it easier to navigate the services they need.”

The Chronic Disease Framework supports government's commitment to building a stronger, more sustainable healthcare system. It also aligns with Live Well PEI and the Provincial Health Plan 2023–2028. 

“The Live Well PEI approach recognizes the many factors that influence health and the importance of reducing barriers to healthy living,” said Chief Public Health Officer Dr. Heather Morrison. “The Chronic Disease Framework builds on this work, creating a shared focus across communities and the healthcare system. Together, we can help prevent chronic disease and support healthier futures for all Islanders.”

Developed with input from Island residents and key partners, the Chronic Disease Framework will guide future initiatives under each pillar. Continued engagement, leadership, and collaboration will support implementation in the years ahead. 

Review the Chronic Disease Framework for Prince Edward Island.

item.title: Islanders are reminded to focus on school bus safety as students return to class next week
item.description:
Islanders are reminded to focus on school bus safety as students return to class next week jenniferdhogan Mon, 08/31/2026 - 11:37

As the school year approaches, the province, local law enforcements agencies, and bus drivers are letting Islanders know that we all have a role to play in keeping kids safe.

Today, a month-long campaign was launched aimed at reminding Island drivers about the rules of the road around school buses, providing helpful tips to students and parents about bus stop safety, and calling on everyone to immediately report incidents to police.

Passing school buses with red lights flashing is a persistent issue reported by bus drivers across the province. Not only is it illegal, but also extremely dangerous, and it puts lives at risk every time it happens.

The campaign encourages parents and educators to talk to children about bus stop safety to help ensure they know all the steps to be as safe as possible getting to and from the bus. Those include arriving early, staying back from the road, looking both ways, and waiting for signal from the driver before crossing the road.

It also shares tips from police on how to report a car passing the school bus illegally. Police suggest noting the plate number, a driver and vehicle description, the location of the incident and the time of day, then calling 9-1-1.

Safety tips will be shared on radio, social media, and print, as well as in classrooms across the province and with parents via direct communication. The campaign will run until the end of September with routine reminders throughout the school year.

To learn more about school bus safety and the rules of the road, visit our website.

Quotes:

“With the school year around the corner, it is paramount that all drivers, parents, and students have the information they need to stay safe around school buses. The more often they are reminded of the potential dangers, the less likely it will be that people put themselves or others in situations with potentially tragic consequences.”

- Minister of Education and Early Years, Robin Croucher

This campaign is an opportunity to remind Islanders that school bus safety is a responsibility that we all share. By stopping for school buses with flashing red lights, slowing down in school zones and reporting dangerous driving, together, we can all help protect students and make our roads safer."

- Minister of Transportation, Infrastructure and Energy, Ernie Hudson

“Local police and our entire justice system takes the enforcement of road safety rules involving school buses very seriously. Report incidents of passing the bus and these will be investigated. Every driver can help by slowing down, exercising care, and following the rules of the road.”

- Minister of Justice and Public Safety, Bloyce Thompson

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
